title: Intermittent API key org-resolution failure during hot config reload affecting Dedicated/Hosted customers
text:
Intermittent API key org-resolution failure during hot config reload affecting Dedicated/Hosted customers

description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers and a subset of Hosted tenants experienced intermittent 401/403 errors for ~18 hours after we deployed a hot config reload that changed org->apikey mappings. Symptoms: requests with valid API keys were sometimes resolved to the wrong org or failed lookup entirely leading to authz failures and request drops. When resolution failed, we returned 401 for token-less routes and 403 for scoped routes. Impact surface: Hosted traffic (5% of production) and dedicated pools in us-west-2. Customer escalations opened by two enterprise customers complaining about increased errors and altered billing attribution. Scope: this bug affects the in-memory apikey resolver cache during config hot reloads that race with background tenant reconciliation jobs. It does not affect private on-prem deployments unless they enabled hot reloads.

root_cause:
During the hot config reload we swap a shared apikey->org mapping pointer without synchronizing in-flight resolver lookups. Concurrent tenant reconciliation writes could interleave, leaving resolver state in a transient mixed view where some keys map to stale org ids and others to the new mapping. Additionally, the resolver had a fast-path that skipped validation for cached entries when a request had a 'tenant-hint' header; that fast-path used the old pointer and produced inconsistent ambiguity on lookups.

mitigation:
1) Rolled back the hot-reload to stop further inconsistent swaps. 2) Applied emergency config to disable tenant-hint fast-paths on the serving nodes. 3) For affected Dedicated customers we initiated manual reconciliation and reissued a small set of API keys where mapping was irrecoverably corrupted. 4) Added an alert to detect sudden spikes in per-tenant 401/403 rate.

resolution_summary:
Patch implemented that makes the apikey resolver swap atomic and adds a short-grace TTL for old mapping reads while new mapping warms. We removed the unsafe fast-path pending a safe refactor. Deployed patch to Hosted first (canary 5%, then 25%, then 100%) and then to Dedicated pools with orchestrated restarts to avoid dual-running pointers. No data exfiltration or privilege escalation was observed. Billing attribution fixes were coordinated with finance and customers have been credited for affected requests.

rollout_plan:
1) Deploy resolver-atomic-swap v1 to canary hosted nodes (5%). Monitor auth error rate and token-mismatch metrics for 30m. 2) If green, expand to 25% for 30m, then 100% hosted. 3) Coordinate with Dedicated operations to schedule rolling restarts of dedicated pools (one pool at a time) and deploy same build. 4) After full rollout, re-enable tenant-hint fast-path behind a feature flag and validate with synthetic tests.

qa_steps:
Create synthetic tenant mapping changes and trigger hot reloads while running high-concurrency lookup traffic to validate no 401 spikes.
Run tenant-reconciliation job concurrently with hot reload to reproduce prior race and assert stable mapping (no mixed-view).
Validate canary and dedicated pools using real-customer-like key sets from staging copy (sanitized).
Run e2e billing attribution smoke to confirm requests are billed to expected orgs after reconciliation.
